confirmed.title: Report claims error status codes did not change, but three error paths moved from 500 to 400
confirmed.evidence: Report line 38 says 'Status codes did not change.' and line 140-141 says 'status codes are unchanged'. Running ca05-probe/status-probe.mts on base 8a070bf vs HEAD: malformed JSON POST /api/lessons 500 → 400 bad-request; bad MIDI bytes on /api/lessons/import/midi throws an uncaught string on base (bypasses Hono onError; a 500 under node-server, inferred) → 400 invalid-midi; PUT /api/lessons/{ref}/fragments/0/notes that empties the lesson 500 → 400 validation (repo.ts Invalid). POST /api/lessons with text/plain is now 415; base mapped every HTTPException to 500 (base app.ts onError).
confirmed.failure_scenario: The API-client note tells the transcriber and agents that only the body shape changed. A client that branches on 500 for bad uploads or malformed requests would now see 400/415 instead. The change is an improvement, but the hand-off note is inaccurate.
confirmed.fix_hint: Reword both sentences: 'malformed-input and invalid-result cases that were 500 are now 400 bad-request/validation (415 for a wrong content type); upsert-replace is 200'.

confirmed.title: 'Failed with exactly those two problems' is not what the mutation produces at HEAD
confirmed.evidence: Reproduced in a scratch copy of HEAD: DELETE description removed and `body(FeedbackInput, undefined)`. vitest listed three problems, including 'POST /api/lessons/{ref}/feedback: binary-only body without a curl example in the description' (rule in app.test.ts OpenAPI completeness test).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Only the report wording is affected. The test does catch the mutation, but a reader trying to reproduce the exact output gets three lines, not two.
confirmed.fix_hint: Drop 'exactly', or list all three messages.

confirmed.title: 415 Unsupported Media Type answers error 'bad-request' but is undocumented
confirmed.evidence: ca05-probe/errshape.mts: POST /api/lessons with content-type text/plain or none → '415 {"error":"bad-request","details":["Unsupported Media Type"]}' (app.ts:151-153 maps any HTTPException < 500 other than 401/404 to bad-request with its own status). The error table lists bad-request only as 400, and no route documents 415.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An agent POSTs JSON without a content-type header and gets a 415 that neither the error table nor the OpenAPI responses mention.
confirmed.fix_hint: Add 415 to the bad-request row (or document it on JSON-body routes).

confirmed.title: After merging main (cfc4381) the new 'hold' key mark is invisible to litKeys and the e2e lit-key regex
confirmed.evidence: main commit cfc4381 (#12/#13, merged 18:16 today, after the report) adds KeyMark 'hold' (PianoKeyboard.tsx renders `pk-${h.mark}`). devtools/api.ts:8 MARKS = ['R','L','next','ok','bad','hint']; types.ts:14 documents the same list; e2e/app.spec.ts:63 regex is /\bpk-(hint|ok|bad|next|R|L)\b/. The merged tree currently passes (41 unit, e2e 21 passed + 1 skipped, bundle clean) because no variant emits 'hold' yet.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Once a variant marks a held-from-earlier key as 'hold', getState().litKeys silently omits it. An agent or test then concludes the key is not shown even though the screen draws it striped.
confirmed.fix_hint: Add 'hold' to MARKS, DevKey docs and the e2e regex when rebasing, or derive the mark from any pk-<mark> class except pk-key/pk-white/pk-black.

confirmed.title: press() validates holdMs only after the keys are already pressed
confirmed.evidence: api.ts:147-150 emits 'on' and player.noteOn for every pitch. Only then does line 154 throw 'holdMs must be a number of milliseconds ≥ 0' for an invalid holdMs. Through the press_keys WebMCP tool the error comes back as { error }, and executeTool does not enforce the schema minimum.

confirmed.fix_hint: Validate holdMs before the press loop.

confirmed.title: reportState doc says state is forgotten on unmount, but a remount with the same key returns the previous mount's state
confirmed.evidence: variantState getter returns variantState.current.state when its key equals `${variant.id}:${lesson.id}:${lesson.updatedAt}`. Switching falling → cards (cards never reports) → falling restores the matching key, and the old object comes back. variant.ts:38 says 'it is forgotten when the variant unmounts'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Once variants adopt reportState, a test that returns to a variant may read the previous mount's step/expected keys until the new mount reports. There is no impact today because no variant calls it.
confirmed.fix_hint: Clear variantState.current when variantKey changes (e.g. in an effect keyed on variantKey), or include a mount counter in the key.

confirmed.title: .mxl upload is a zip bomb: every zip entry is unpacked in memory with no limit, and there is no request-body limit
confirmed.evidence: readMxl calls `files = unzipSync(bytes)` (line 65), which unpacks EVERY entry before container.xml is looked up. readUpload in apps/server/src/app.ts:617-628 reads the whole body with `c.req.arrayBuffer()` / `parseBody()` and has no size cap. Probe bomb.ts + bombrun.ts: a 512,192-byte zip with 5 × 100 MB zero files → musicxmlToLesson took 1211 ms; RSS went from 98 to 623 MB, arrayBuffers 527 MB; then it threw 'The .mxl archive contains no MusicXML score'. HTTP: POST /api/lessons/import/musicxml with that file → 400 after 1.28 s. docker-compose.yml:27 defaults `API_TOKEN: ${PIANO_STEPS_API_TOKEN:-}` (empty), and its header documents `PIANO_STEPS_BIND=0.0.0.0` for using an iPad on Wi-Fi.
confirmed.failure_scenario: In the documented LAN setup with no token, any device on the Wi-Fi POSTs a ~5 MB .mxl containing ~5 GB of zeros, or a few 512 KB ones in parallel. The Node process blocks the event loop and allocates gigabytes, then gets OOM-killed or stalls every other request. A body limit alone does not fix this: the ratio is about 1000×.
confirmed.fix_hint: Use `unzipSync(bytes, { filter: f => f.name === 'META-INF/container.xml' || f.name === rootPath })` (two passes, or a filter by .xml/.musicxml name), reject any entry whose `originalSize` exceeds a cap (for example 20 MB), and add `hono/body-limit` to both import routes.

confirmed.title: MusicXML <transpose> is ignored, so transposing-instrument parts import at the written pitch, not the sounding pitch
confirmed.evidence: The `attributes` case (lines 203-216) reads divisions, staves and time only. Pitch is computed at line 253 as `(octave + 1) * 12 + step + alter`, with no transpose offset. Probe mx1.ts: a Bb clarinet part (`<transpose><diatonic>-1</diatonic><chromatic>-2</chromatic>`) with written D5 → imported pitch 74 (sounding is 72). A guitar part (`<octave-change>-1</octave-change>`, which MuseScore writes for guitar) with written E4 → imported 64 (sounding is 52).
confirmed.failure_scenario: A user imports a melody from a lead sheet or part for Bb clarinet/trumpet, Eb alto sax, or guitar. Every note is silently off by a major 2nd, a major 6th or an octave. The lesson teaches the wrong keys and passes validation.
confirmed.fix_hint: Track `chromatic + 12 * octave-change` (plus `<double/>`) from `<transpose>` per part/staff, and add it to the pitch.

confirmed.title: MusicXML fragment cuts are rounded to 3 decimals while note onsets keep 4, so a fragment's downbeat note is filed under the previous fragment
confirmed.evidence: measureFragments uses `r3(cuts[k])` (lines 385-386); note starts use `r(...)` with 4 decimals (line 337). Membership is half-open with eps 1e-6, both in notesInRange (steps.ts:33) and repo.replaceFragmentNotes (repo.ts:180). Probe mx2.ts, 4/4, one quarter per beat: 72 bpm → `[0,6.667) → C5 D5 E5 F5 C5 D5 E5 F5 C5 | [6.667,13.333) → D5 E5 F5 …`, because the downbeat at 6.6667 < 6.667. The same happens at 66 bpm (cut 7.273) and 90 bpm (cut 10.667). 100 bpm is fine.
confirmed.failure_scenario: For any score whose bar length in seconds rounds up at the 4th decimal (e.g. 66/72/90 bpm), fragment N+1 starts without its downbeat, and fragment N ends with an extra note. An agent asked to fix 'fragment #2' via PUT /fragments/1/notes never touches that downbeat, because replaceFragmentNotes treats it as part of fragment #1.
confirmed.fix_hint: Round cuts with `r` (4 dp), the same grid as note starts, or snap each cut to the onset of the first note at that bar. Pre-existing and outside this branch: autoFragments (steps.ts:97, `round` to 3 dp) has the same mismatch for MIDI/JSON lessons with a tempo.

confirmed.title: An API token with a non-Latin-1 character locks the web app into offline demo mode and hides the token field
confirmed.evidence: `call()` adds `authorization: Bearer ${t}` to EVERY request, including GETs (api.ts:49). The Settings field stores raw input on every keystroke: `onChange={(e) => api.setApiToken(e.target.value.trim() || null)}` (App.tsx:343). The field is shown only when `health?.auth` (App.tsx:334), and health is fetched once via call() (App.tsx:63). listLessons treats any non-ApiError as offline (api.ts:93-96). Probe hdr.mjs: `fetch(url, {headers:{authorization:'Bearer abc​'}})` → Chromium `TypeError … String contains non ISO-8859-1 code point`, WebKit `TypeError: Type error`. Node: same TypeError for 'Bearer токен'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The owner pastes a token carrying a zero-width space, or types it with the Ukrainian layout active. Every fetch then throws TypeError. On the next load, getHealth fails → health=null → the API token field disappears from Settings; listLessons sets offline=true → only the 3 built-in demo lessons show, and nothing points to the token. The only way out is clearing site data. Not verified: whether iPadOS allows a Cyrillic keyboard in a password field; the paste path does not depend on that.
confirmed.fix_hint: Wrap the fetch in call() so a TypeError becomes an ApiError (status 0) with a clear message. Reject or strip non-printable/non-Latin-1 characters in setApiToken. Show the token field whenever getApiToken() is non-null, regardless of health. Consider sending the token only on non-GET requests (the server ignores it on GETs).

confirmed.title: export.mid → import/midi does not give 'the same notes back' as the OpenAPI description promises
confirmed.evidence: Spec text at app.ts:454-455: 'Re-importing it with /api/lessons/import/midi gives the same notes back.' lessonToMidi always writes two tracks, even an empty 'Left hand' one (midi.ts:95-100). midiToLesson drops empty tracks (midi.ts:21) and then splits a single track at C4 (midi.ts:25-37); it also trims leading silence > 50 ms and then drops the time signature (midi.ts:49-60). HTTP test on my port-9396 server: created rv-melody (all R: 67@0.5, 62@1, 57@1.5, 55@2, 4/4) → GET export.mid → POST import/midi → `[(67,0,'R'),(62,0.5,'R'),(57,1,'L'),(55,1.5,'L')] {'bpm':120}`. Probe rt2.ts: overlapping same-pitch notes in one hand (C4 0–2 + C4 1–1.5) come back as 0–1.5 and 1–2. Demo lessons do round-trip exactly (rt.ts).
confirmed.failure_scenario: An agent follows the documented export → edit → re-import workflow on a melody-only lesson that dips below middle C, or on a lesson starting with a rest. The lesson silently changes: those notes switch to the left hand, every onset shifts earlier, and the bar grid is lost.
confirmed.fix_hint: Have midiToLesson honour the track names it writes ('Right hand'/'Left hand') and keep a single named track's hand; skip the leading-silence trim when the file came from lessonToMidi (or only trim when the first event is > 1 bar). Or narrow the spec text to what actually holds.

confirmed.title: The MusicXML importer slows down quadratically with many tempo changes and blocks the event loop
confirmed.evidence: `toSec` scans every tempo segment with no early break (`for (const x of segs) if (x.q <= q + EPS) s = x;`, lines 310-314). It is called twice per note and once per bar line, all before the 20,000-note validation limit. measureFragments adds `notes.some` for each cut (line 387). Probe cpu.ts (one `<sound tempo>` + one note per measure): 10k measures / 1.3 MB → 1134 ms; 20k / 2.7 MB → 2046 ms; 40k / 5.4 MB → 7760 ms, which is then rejected anyway for having more than 20,000 notes.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An 11–20 MB MusicXML file with a tempo mark in every bar freezes the single Node process for 30 s to minutes. All other API and web requests hang. Combined with the missing body limit, it needs only write access, and the default LAN setup has no token.
confirmed.fix_hint: Binary-search the segments (or walk notes in sorted order with a moving index), and stop parsing once the note count exceeds the 20,000 limit.

confirmed.title: A tie chain is broken by a same-pitch note in another voice, which turns into a spurious re-attack
confirmed.evidence: The tie key is `${staff}:${pitch}` with no voice (line 265), and any untied note at that key runs `open.delete(key)` (line 284). Probe mx6.ts (2/4): voice 1 has G4 tie-start at beat 2; after a backup, voice 2 has an untied G4 half note; bar 2 has voice 1 G4 tie-stop → output `[67,0,2],[72,0,1],[67,1,1],…,[67,2,2]`. Expected: one G4 from 1 to 4 s in voice 1.
confirmed.failure_scenario: In piano music where an inner voice shares a pitch with a tied melody note, the import shows a repeated key press the user should not make. The lesson is still accepted.
confirmed.fix_hint: Include `<voice>` in the tie key (e.g. `${staff}:${voice}:${pitch}`), and only delete chains for the note's own voice.

confirmed.title: .mxl container handling differs from plain files: a UTF-16 rootfile is rejected and a './' full-path is not resolved
confirmed.evidence: readMxl decodes the score with `strFromU8(file)` (UTF-8 only, line 81) instead of `decodeText` (BOM-aware, lines 55-60), and looks up `files[path]` verbatim (line 79). Probe mx3.ts: the same UTF-16LE+BOM score imports as a plain file → `[{pitch:60,…}]`, but inside an .mxl → 'Not valid XML: char '�' is not expected'. A container `full-path="./score.musicxml"` → 'The .mxl archive contains no MusicXML score'. A normal UTF-8 .mxl with a rootfile in a subfolder plus a PDF rootfile imports fine (mx7.ts).
confirmed.failure_scenario: An exporter that writes UTF-16 MusicXML (the reason decodeText exists) inside .mxl, or writes './'-relative rootfile paths, gets a 400 for a valid score.
confirmed.fix_hint: Use decodeText(file) in readMxl; normalise the full-path (strip a leading './', decode %20); fall back to scanning for a .musicxml/.xml entry when the container path is missing.

confirmed.title: An XML encoding declaration other than UTF-8/UTF-16 is ignored, so the title is garbled
confirmed.evidence: decodeText checks the BOM only, then decodes as UTF-8 (lines 55-60). Probe mx3.ts: a file with `encoding="ISO-8859-1"` and the title byte 0xFC → title "F�r Elise". Notes are unaffected.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An older Finale/Sibelius Latin-1 export imports with garbled title and composer, and the slug is derived from the garbled title.
confirmed.fix_hint: Read the encoding from the XML declaration and pass it to TextDecoder (fall back to UTF-8).

confirmed.title: pianoSteps.press() validates holdMs after it has already pressed the keys
confirmed.evidence: Lines 147-150 emit `input.emit('on', p, 'sim')` and `player.noteOn(p)` for every pitch. The holdMs check `if (!(holdMs >= 0)) throw …` runs only at line 154 (read from source, not executed).
confirmed.failure_scenario: `press([60], -5)`, or the WebMCP press_keys tool with holdMs -5 (the JSON schema minimum is advisory), throws or returns {error}. Key 60 stays held, so later getState()/e2e assertions see a stuck key.
confirmed.fix_hint: Validate holdMs before the emit loop.

confirmed.title: lessonToMidi writes a wrong tempo for bpm below about 3.6, so the exported note times are wrong
confirmed.evidence: `midi.header.setTempo(lesson.tempo?.bpm ?? 120)` with no clamp. The schema allows any positive bpm (lesson.ts:57). Probe rt3.ts: bpm 2 → re-import reports bpm 4.5376 and the note at 3 s comes back at 1.3223 s; bpm 3 → 18.6174. The microseconds-per-quarter value overflows MIDI's 24-bit field.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A lesson with a nonsense low tempo (for example from a transcription bug) exports a .mid whose timing is wrong in any DAW or on re-import.
confirmed.fix_hint: Clamp the tempo to the MIDI-representable range (about 3.58 to 60,000,000 bpm), or write 120 when it is out of range.

confirmed.title: The first tempo mark is applied back to the start, overriding the MusicXML default of 120 for the earlier bars
confirmed.evidence: `if (!tempos.length || tempos[0][0] > EPS) tempos.unshift([0, tempos[0]?.[1] ?? DEFAULT_BPM])`. Probe mx6.ts: no tempo in bars 1-2, `<sound tempo="60"/>` at bar 3 → notes `[72,0,4],[74,4,4],[76,8,4]`, i.e. bars 1-2 at 60 bpm instead of 120. This is a heuristic choice; the log's 'no tempo → 120' (log.md:60) covers scores with no mark at all.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A score whose opening tempo is text only ('Allegro') with a metronome mark later ('Più mosso ♩=160' at bar 17) imports its first 16 bars at 160 bpm.
confirmed.fix_hint: Start from DEFAULT_BPM at q=0 when the first mark is later, or document the heuristic in the route description.

confirmed.title: devtools e2e asserts exact litKeys that only the placeholder variant produces; fails once feat/1 (falling) is on main
confirmed.evidence: Trial merge (main cfc4381 + feat/1 + feat/2 + feat/3 + feat/5), `E2E_WEB_PORT=9396 E2E_API_PORT=9397 npx playwright test` → `3 failed, 1 skipped, 18 passed`. Failures: [ipad-webkit] devtools.spec.ts:5, [desktop-chromium] devtools.spec.ts:5 (line 11: Received + "C3" vs ['C4','E4','G4']), [desktop-chromium] devtools.spec.ts:46 (line 63: Received + "C3", + "E4" vs ['D4','F#4']). A scratch probe on the same tree showed for ui=falling: idle litKeys [C3:next, E4:next]; after press(['C4','E4',67]) [C3:next, C4:hint, E4:next, G4:hint]; after release() [C3:next, E4:next]; press('A3',100) [C3:next, A3:hint, E4:next]. So lines 11, 14 (`toEqual([])`) and 17 (`toEqual([57])`) all fail, plus line 63. Cause: falling/marks.ts:34-35 puts a `next` outline on the upcoming step even when idle, and devtools/api.ts:8 counts `next` as lit. Control run, feat/5 alone on cfc4381 (placeholder variants): `21 passed, 1 skipped`. The run on the pre-#12 main (27c747c) gave the same 3 failures.
confirmed.failure_scenario: When feat/1 and feat/5 are both on main, in either merge order, the new `e2e` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml fails deterministically (CI retries=1 does not help), so the second PR cannot get the green CI that AGENTS.md requires. `npm run e2e` locally is red the same way. The other variants would not fix it if the test were pinned to them: cards idles with [C3:L, E4:R], and sheet keeps the last released key lit as 'hint' for PROBE_MS=2500 (sheet/index.tsx:21), so line 14 fails there too.
confirmed.fix_hint: Assert on the pressed keys, not exact equality. For example, `expect(held.litKeys.map(k=>k.name)).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(['C4','E4','G4']))`, or filter `litKeys` to `mark==='hint'`/`ok`/`bad`. After release(), assert that heldKeys is [] and that the released pitches carry no hint/ok/bad mark. Apply the same change at lines 17 and 63. Also update the report's merge note to point at devtools.spec.ts.

confirmed.title: Dev API litKeys ignores main's new 'hold' key mark (#12, cfc4381)
confirmed.evidence: devtools/api.ts:8 `const MARKS = ['R', 'L', 'next', 'ok', 'bad', 'hint'];`, and litKeys() (api.ts:236-243) only reports keys whose class matches one of these. Main now has `| 'hold' // still held from an earlier step` at `git show main:apps/web/src/ui/PianoKeyboard.tsx` line 13, with `.pk-white.pk-hold` at PianoKeyboard.css:99. docs/testing-api.md:51 lists the marks without 'hold'. The e2e regex at e2e/app.spec.ts:63 `/\bpk-(hint|ok|bad|next|R|L)\b/` also lacks it. A grep for `'hold'|pk-hold` in the three variant worktrees matches only the rebased shared PianoKeyboard, so no variant emits 'hold' yet. Typecheck passes because DevKey.mark is `string` (devtools/types.ts:15).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Once a variant adopts #12's 'hold' mark (a note held over from an earlier step), getState().litKeys and the WebMCP get_state/press_keys results silently leave those keys out. An agent or a test that reads 'what the screen shows' then sees fewer lit keys than are drawn.
confirmed.fix_hint: Add 'hold' to MARKS (better: derive the list from the KeyMark type in ui/PianoKeyboard.tsx). Optionally report the `next` ring overlay (KeyHighlight.next / `.pk-ring`) too. Update docs/testing-api.md:51 and the regex at e2e/app.spec.ts:63.

confirmed.title: litKeys cannot tell user-held keys from a variant's own 'hint' marks (sheet keeps a released key lit 2.5 s)
confirmed.evidence: Scratch probe on the combined tree with ui=sheet: after press(['C4','E4',67]) then release(), heldKeys=[] but litKeys=[G4] at +0, +50, +200, +500 and +1500 ms; a single press('D4') then release() also left D4 lit after 500 ms. The source is sheet/index.tsx:216 `if (pr) marks.set(pr.pitch, { mark: pr.hand ?? 'hint' })`, with PROBE_MS = 2500 at line 21: the last pressed key is intentionally shown for 2.5 s.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A future e2e or agent check that does press → release → `litKeys` is empty on the sheet tab fails, or passes only after waiting more than 2.5 s. The `hint` mark is used both for 'user is holding this' and for the sheet's 'where this key sits on the staff' probe.
confirmed.fix_hint: Document in docs/testing-api.md that `heldKeys` is the source of truth for presses and that `litKeys` includes variant decorations. Optionally have variants publish their probe/expected keys through reportState.
